concepts.title: Properties of Acids and Bases
concepts.definition: Acids are substances that taste sour and have an acidic chemical nature, while bases are substances that taste bitter, feel soapy to the touch, and have a basic chemical nature.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Acids are indeed sour; bases are both bitter and soapy.
question_patterns: what are the characteristics of acids
how do bases feel when touched
identify the nature of a substance based on taste
distinguish between acidic and basic substances

solution_steps.explain: Acids taste sour; bases taste bitter and feel soapy.

concepts.title: Indicators
concepts.definition: In brief, Indicators are special substances that change their color when exposed to acidic or basic solutions, allowing us to identify their chemical nature without tasting them.
concepts.key_idea: Indicators signal acidity or basicity through color change.
question_patterns: how do indicators help identify substances
what happens to litmus in an acidic solution

solution_steps.explain: Litmus turns red in acid and blue in base.

concepts.title: Neutralisation Reaction
concepts.definition: In brief, Neutralisation is a chemical process where an acid and a base react to form both salt and water, releasing heat in the process.
concepts.key_idea: Acid and base cancel each other's effects to create both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both salt and water.
question_patterns: what are the products of a neutralisation reaction
calculate the outcome of mixing acid and base

solution_steps.explain: Acid and base are mixed in suitable amounts.
Heat is evolved during the reaction.

solution_template.explain: Neutralisation occurs between HCl and NaOH.
The reaction produces sodium chloride (salt) and water.
